disposition_reason: Mechanistic field study of three clonal trees of a high-Cd cultivar (NA 312) at the International Cocoa Genebank, Trinidad, reporting nib and testa Cd (mean ± SD and by fruit maturity) alongside root, branch, leaf, pod husk and soil Cd, isotope fractionation, speciation and whole-tree mass balance. Primary is a Marker markdown conversion (no PDF in library).
disposition_locator: Table 1 (nibs) and Table 2 (all organs); Results 'Cd accumulation and partitioning'

study.material_scope: fresh nibs and testae from immature, intermediate and mature pods; other organs as context
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Grown at International Cocoa Genebank Trinidad (ICGT), Centeno, Trinidad; research field collection, not commercial
study.sampling_unit: three genetically identical trees (rooted cuttings T2, T4, T6); 5 pods across maturity stages (nib n=5, testa n=4)
study.method: HNO3 open-block digestion (8 h, 130 °C) of 50 mg, ICP-MS (Agilent 7700x)/ICP-OES; MC-ICP-MS isotopes after microwave digestion; XANES; LA-ICP-MS
study.basis: dry weight (fresh tissues separated, oven-dried at 65 °C; Table 1 header 'DW')
study.qa: Cd recovery 89-91% for BCR-142R soil, NIST 1573a tomato leaves and NIST 2384 baking chocolate (Table S1); isotope blank <1.07%

findings.basis: dry weight (fresh tissues separated, oven-dried at 65 °C; Table 1 header 'DW')
findings.notes: Fresh, unfermented fruit tissue from NA 312 (Nanay group), a cultivar selected for high Cd accumulation, ICGT Centeno, Trinidad; three clonal trees (T2, T4, T6) on acidic soil (pH 4.1, aqua-regia topsoil Cd 0.22 mg/kg). Not representative of commercial beans. SD calculated from biological replicates per table note.

controls.control: Breeding low-Cd cultivars / grafting onto low-Cd rootstocks (pathway evidence: nib Cd sourced from branch phloem rather than leaf remobilization)
controls.comparator: isotope fractionation between organs of one high-Cd genotype
controls.outcome: Δ114/110Cd nib-branch -0.08 ± 0.06 ‰ (not distinguishable) vs IF3 leaves-nib 0.25 ± 0.05 ‰; branches hold 57% of tree Cd (stem 21%, roots 14%, leaves 9%, fruit <1%). Authors note the scion may be the main regulator of nib Cd, so rootstock grafting efficacy needs validation. No bean-Cd reduction tested.
controls.locator: Abstract; Results (mass balance, isotopes, Table 3); Discussion implications

controls.control: Context: soil acidity and low organic carbon raise Cd bioavailability; high-accumulator genotype amplifies nib Cd
controls.outcome: Topsoil pH 4.1, SOC 1.9%, aqua-regia Cd 0.22 ± 0.05 mg/kg, 29% Ca(NO3)2-extractable (0.08 mg/kg); leaf IF2/soil transfer factor 12.5 vs 4.5 average in Ecuador survey; nibs ~2 mg/kg exceed 'typical trade limits of 0.6 mg Cd kg-1'.
controls.locator: Results 'Characterization of the cacao-soil system'; Discussion

controls.control: Context for post-harvest mitigation: nib Cd mainly O-ligand bound (likely phytate), testa Cd O(C)-ligand bound
controls.outcome: Nib 60-90% O-ligands (phytate most plausible; phytate/Cd molar ratio 1300); testa 100% O(C)-ligands. Authors say this informs fermentation-stage Cd mobilization research; no mitigation tested.
Fruit Cd mass: pod husk 0.62 ± 0.15, nib 0.29 ± 0.13, testa 0.06 ± 0.02, placenta 0.03 ± 0.01; testa concentration (2.36 mg/kg) similar to nib (2.05 mg/kg) in fresh tissue.
controls.locator: Results 'Cd accumulation and partitioning'; Figure S4

regulatory.status: cited as range 0.10-0.80 mg/kg by product; no individual product value given

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary gives no nib or testa concentrations; primary Table 2 reports nib 2.05 ± 0.42 mg/kg (n=5; mature 1.75 ± 0.08) and testa 2.36 ± 0.43 mg/kg (n=4).
Stored lists ingredient [[ingredients/chocolate]]; no chocolate or processed product was analysed (fresh fruit tissues only).

Stored repeats 'tissue-to-soil concentration factors ranged from 10 to 28'; from the paper's own values the nib/aqua-regia topsoil ratio is 2.05/0.22 = 9.3 (or 7.3 using total Cd 0.28), slightly below the stated lower bound of 10.
Stored summary does not mention the testa/pod-husk duplicate row or the Table 1 vs Table 2 nib mean difference.
unresolved: Primary is a Marker markdown conversion; the duplicated mature testa row (2.46 ± 1.20 = mature pod husk) cannot be checked against the original PDF table.
Per-tree nib/testa values for mature pods (n=3) are not printed in the main text.
